suites_file.name: suites.yaml
suites_file.text:
# Two suites of tests for Personal I, on the class assistant (Wren, for Morgan
# Reyes: fictional). A worked example for Skill Eval Lite's checks-only mode:
#
#     python3 run_ab.py suite examples/personal-suites/suites.yaml --out runs/personal-suites
#
# Each suite's items are folders under product/, stage/ or process/; its
# control cases are folders under controls/<suite>/, each with expect.json;
# its tests' files are under tests/<test>/. Paths are relative to this file.
schema: skill-eval-lite/suites@1
title: Board drafts and how Wren prepares a brief

suites:
  - id: board-drafts
    object: product
    what: >
      Drafts that Wren writes for the Riverside board or its finance committee,
      which Morgan sends under their own name. Six real drafts, made by the
      class assistant's demonstration runs on 2026-10-26.
    file: output.md
    items: [summary-1, summary-2, summary-3, summary-4, note-1, note-2]
    tests:
      - id: no-shorthand
        kind: mechanical
        question: Does the committee's shorthand (Q1, cttee, mtg) reach a board document?
        criterion: Passes when none of Q1, cttee or mtg appears in the draft.
        why: A program can settle whether a string appears; a person would miss one.
        check: {kind: not-contains, text: ["Q1", "cttee", "mtg"]}
      - id: facts-match-the-source
        kind: llm
        question: Does every date, amount, name and decision in the draft match its source?
        criterion: >
          Passes when every date, amount, name and decision in the draft can be
          found in the source (the notes or the email) or the request, unchanged.
          A fact that is added, changed or contradicted fails. Unknown when the
          source can't settle it.
        why: Matching facts across two documents needs reading, not a pattern.
        prompt: tests/facts-match-the-source/prompt.md
        model: claude-sonnet-5-5
        decision: The last line of the response is PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN.
      - id: sendable
        kind: human
        form: rating
        question: Would Morgan send this draft as it is?
        criterion: A rating from 1 to 4 on the scale below; 3 or 4 counts as a pass.
        why: Whether a draft is sendable depends on taste and on knowing the audience.
        pass_at: 3
        scale:
          1: "Morgan would rewrite it: wrong, missing what was asked, or not in Morgan's voice."
          2: "It needs substantial edits: a wrong fact, a missing section, or the wrong register."
          3: "Small edits only: a phrase or a line Morgan would change."
          4: "Morgan would send it as it is."
        instructions: tests/sendable/instructions.md

  - id: graph-briefs
    object: process
    what: >
      How Wren prepares a brief about a person or a funder: whether it looks
      things up in the knowledge graph before it writes, and writes only what
      it found. Four real runs from the class assistant's demonstrations, two
      of them made with the knowledge graph removed.
    items: [dana-brief-1, dana-brief-2, priya-brief-1, priya-brief-2]
    tests:
      - id: search-before-write
        kind: mechanical
        question: Did the run look something up in the knowledge graph before it wrote the brief?
        criterion: >
          Passes when a step that searched or read the graph (kb/kb search, node
          or query, or the knowledge-graph skill), in a step that didn't fail,
          comes before the first step that wrote a file.
        why: The order of steps in a record is something a program can check exactly.
        program: tests/search-before-write/check.py
      - id: steps-follow
        kind: llm
        question: Does each step follow from what the step before it found, and does the brief use only what the steps found?
        criterion: >
          Passes when the lookups come before the writing, each step makes sense
          given what the previous ones returned, and every fact in the brief was
          returned by a step or given in the request. Fails when the brief states
          something no step found, or was written before the lookups.
        why: Whether a step follows from a result needs reading the results.
        prompt: tests/steps-follow/prompt.md
        model: claude-sonnet-5-5
        decision: The last line of the response is PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN.
      - id: sound-process
        kind: human
        form: rating
        question: Would you trust a brief made this way?
        criterion: A rating from 1 to 4 on the scale below; 3 or 4 counts as a pass.
        why: Trust in a process is a judgment about what was checked and what was assumed.
        pass_at: 3
        scale:
          1: "No: it wrote without looking, or claims what its steps didn't find."
          2: "Barely: it looked, but the brief goes beyond what it found."
          3: "Mostly: it looked first, with a step or two that wasted time or failed."
          4: "Yes: it looked up what it needed first, and wrote only that."
        instructions: tests/sound-process/instructions.md

# What this draft was for

Wren, Morgan Reyes's assistant (fictional), was asked:

> Here are my notes from Thursday's Riverside finance committee meeting
> (input/committee-notes.md). Turn them into a short summary I can send to the
> committee: what we decided, who does what by when, and what is still open.
> Save it in drafts/.

The draft goes to the Riverside board or its finance committee under Morgan's name.

## The source: input/committee-notes.md

Riverside finance cttee - Thu 5 Nov 2026, 6:30pm, video

Present: me (chair), Ellis, Tom Becker, Alicia Moreno

Q1 actuals (Jul-Sep)
- revenue roughly on plan
- program supplies over by ~6,500. Camp supplies for next summer bought in Sept?
  Ellis to confirm timing vs real overspend
- 2 Sept lines miscoded. Ellis sends corrected Q1 actuals by Tue 10 Nov

Audit
- auditor wants fieldwork in Jan, not March
- Ellis not happy about Jan (two staff out). Ellis to ask auditor about Feb
- no decision

Reserve transfer
- Tom suggested moving 5,000 from operating reserve to cover supplies
- not ours to decide, goes to full board 19 Nov
- Alicia wants a one-page explanation for the board first

Packet
- me: cover memo draft to Ellis by Wed 11 Nov
- packet to board Thu 12 Nov (one week before mtg)

Next cttee mtg Thu 3 Dec

Subject: Finance committee summary - Thursday 5 Nov [DATE UNVERIFIED]

Hello all,

Thanks for making time Thursday evening. I know this is unpaid time on top of a full week. Here is where we landed.

What we decided

1. The reserve transfer is not ours to decide. Tom suggested moving 5,000 [UNVERIFIED] from the operating reserve to cover program supplies. That goes to the full board on 19 Nov.
2. The packet goes to the board on Thu 12 Nov, one week before the meeting.

Who does what by when

1. Ellis: send corrected Q1 actuals (July to September) by Tue 10 Nov. Two September lines were coded to the wrong account.
2. Ellis: confirm whether the program supplies overage is a timing issue or a real overspend.
3. Ellis: ask the auditor whether fieldwork can happen in February instead of January.
4. Morgan: send the cover memo draft to Ellis by Wed 11 Nov.

What is still open

1. Program supplies are over plan by about 6,500 [UNVERIFIED]. Camp supplies for next summer may have been bought in September, which would make this timing and not overspend. Ellis is checking.
2. Audit fieldwork timing. The auditor wants January. Nothing is decided until Ellis hears back on February.
3. One-page explanation of the reserve transfer for the board. Alicia asked for it ahead of the 19 Nov meeting. Who writes it is not settled.

Revenue for Q1 was roughly on plan.

Next committee meeting is Thu 3 Dec.

Thanks,
Morgan

What happened

1. First quarter (July to September): revenue is roughly on plan. Program supplies are over budget by about 6,500 [UNVERIFIED - figure from meeting notes, before Ellis's corrected actuals]. Two September lines were miscoded, so that number may change.

# Draft: page-one note, Riverside Q1 finance packet

To: Ellis Park
Status: DRAFT for Morgan to review. Not sent.
Register: Riverside board (volunteer audience, unpaid time). Board memo register is unverified per voice.md.

---

Hello all,

One item to read before the numbers. Program supplies came in 6,200 [UNVERIFIED - not checked against the Q1 actuals or the approved budget line] over budget for the first quarter (July to September).

This is a timing difference, not new spending. In September we bought next summer's camp supplies early to get a bulk discount. That cost landed in this quarter, and we would otherwise have paid it next spring. [UNVERIFIED - confirm the purchase total, the discount, and the invoice date with Ellis.]

If you have questions on this before the meeting, send them to me or Ellis. I know this lands in a heavy week, and I appreciate your time.

Morgan

---

## Notes for Morgan (not part of the draft)

1. The 6,200 comes from you, not from a document. I found no Riverside actuals or budget file in this repo (no Riverside/ folder), so I could not check it. Ellis supplies the quarter's actuals; the packet's variance line is the source to match.
2. The bulk-discount reason is also from you. If the packet can show the purchase (amount, date, discount), add one number so the board can see the timing claim for itself.
3. Question: in which quarter would the camp supplies have been bought otherwise, and will that quarter come in under budget by the same amount? If yes, one sentence saying so is what makes this "timing" and not "overspend".
4. Ellis's email is dated 12 November and says the packet goes out tonight. Today is 26 October by my calendar, and the board meets 19 November per the graph. Worth a glance at which date is right.

You will see board drafts one at a time, each with what it was for and the

plainly and briefly, puts the decision first in anything for the board,

tests.question: Did the run look something up in the knowledge graph before it wrote the brief?
tests.criterion: Passes when a step that searched or read the graph (kb/kb search, node or query, or the knowledge-graph skill), in a step that didn't fail, comes before the first step that wrote a file.
tests.why: The order of steps in a record is something a program can check exactly.

tests.question: Does each step follow from what the step before it found, and does the brief use only what the steps found?
tests.criterion: Passes when the lookups come before the writing, each step makes sense given what the previous ones returned, and every fact in the brief was returned by a step or given in the request. Fails when the brief states something no step found, or was written before the lookups.
tests.why: Whether a step follows from a result needs reading the results.
tests.decision: The last line of the response is PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN.
tests.prompt_text:
You are checking how an assistant prepared a brief. Below are what it was
asked and its standing rule, the brief it wrote (output.md), and the trace of
its run: every step in order, what each step was, and the start of what it
returned.

Question: does each step follow from what the steps before it found, and does
the brief use only what the steps found?

- The lookups should come before the writing.
- A failed or wasted step is not a failure by itself; a brief that states
  something no step returned, and the request didn't give, is.
- A brief written before the lookups that support it fails.

Give two or three sentences of reasons, naming the steps you mean by number.
Then, on the last line, write only PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN.

{{case}}

tests.question: Would you trust a brief made this way?
tests.criterion: A rating from 1 to 4 on the scale below; 3 or 4 counts as a pass.
tests.why: Trust in a process is a judgment about what was checked and what was assumed.

scale.1: No: it wrote without looking, or claims what its steps didn't find.
scale.2: Barely: it looked, but the brief goes beyond what it found.
scale.3: Mostly: it looked first, with a step or two that wasted time or failed.
scale.4: Yes: it looked up what it needed first, and wrote only that.

tests.instructions_text:
# Sound process: instructions for raters

You will see runs one at a time: what the assistant was asked, its standing
rule (search the knowledge graph before writing about a person or funder),
the steps it took in order with the start of what each returned, and the
brief it wrote. They are in a random order, and nothing says where each came
from.

For each, decide: **would you trust a brief made this way?**

| Rating | Means | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | It looked up what it needed first, and wrote only that. | Searches, reads the two pages the brief uses, then writes. |
| 3 | It looked first, with a step or two that wasted time or failed. | A refused attempt to read a folder outside its own, then the right lookups. |
| 2 | It looked, but the brief goes beyond what it found. | The brief gives a figure that no step returned. |
| 1 | It wrote without looking, or claims what its steps didn't find. | Writes the brief first and searches afterwards. |

Read what each step returned, not only its name: a search that returned
"No such file" did not find anything. Give a one-line reason for each rating,
and judge on your own.
